claims.claim: **Assessment hunts for serious, treatable causes:** trauma, stroke, mass lesions, toxin ingestion, and CNS infection or inflammation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The commonest cause is post-infectious acute cerebellar ataxia**, which settles on its own and is **a diagnosis of exclusion.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mimics:** weakness or pain can cause an unsteady gait, and a frightened or very unwell child may appear ataxic.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ataxia** is unsteadiness, imbalance or clumsiness from uncoordinated muscle movement, affecting gait, speech or motor skills. **Acute = under 72 hours in a previously well child.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Vascular causes may need urgent lysis** — see the Stroke guideline.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Post-infectious acute cerebellar ataxia** (viral — varicella, EBV, HHV6, enteroviruses — or *Mycoplasma*): most commonly **5–10 days after a prodromal illness**, typically in children **2–7 years**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Its course:** cerebellar features are **worst at the start**, typically getting better within **48–72 hours**; most recover fully in **10–21 days** (over 90% resolve by 2 months).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Toxins** (antihistamines, antiepileptics, ethanol/ethylene glycol/isopropyl, sedative-hypnotics): variable and dose-related; ask about environmental exposure, medications the child could reach, or a recent medication change; look for **altered GCS or a toxidrome.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tumours** (via haemorrhage, oedema or obstructive hydrocephalus): acute or acute-on-chronic; **conscious level is usually normal**, with raised ICP features, constitutional symptoms or focal deficits.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Trauma** (haemorrhage, contusion, diffuse axonal injury, concussion): acute or chronic; look for a history or signs of head injury and **risk factors for non-accidental injury.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ADEM** (autoimmune CNS demyelination): typically **1–4 weeks after a febrile illness**, with lethargy or irritability and multiple deficits — pyramidal signs, optic neuritis, hemiplegia, ataxia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **History:** time course (acute under 72 hours); antecedent viral illness, rash, head trauma or earache; drug, toxin or environmental exposures.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A thorough neurological examination is essential**, including conscious state; **exclude meningoencephalitis** (fever, meningism).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Localise it.** Cerebellar: dysdiadochokinesis, dysmetria, dysarthria, tremor, nystagmus, staggering or wide-based gait. Sensory: positive Romberg, hyporeflexia, lost proprioception, vibration and light touch. Vestibular: nystagmus without other cerebellar signs.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Red flags:** altered conscious state · raised intracranial pressure · meningism · focal neurology · weakness · abnormal deep tendon reflexes · lost vibration sense, proprioception or tactile discrimination.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If features fit post-infectious acute cerebellar ataxia, no investigations may be needed.** Investigate if ataxia **persists beyond 72 hours, gets worse at any point after onset**, or another cause is suspected.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Then consider:** blood glucose, venous blood gas, electrolytes, LFTs, anticonvulsant level and ethanol; CT or MRI; toxicology, metabolic screen, viral studies, vitamin B12, EEG — and **lumbar puncture only after neuroimaging.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treatment depends on cause**; post-infectious acute cerebellar ataxia generally needs **no treatment.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the local paediatric team** for acute ataxia of unclear cause, or any chronic or recurrent ataxia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider transfer** for other focal neurological signs, raised ICP, a history atypical for post-infectious ataxia or unclear cause, or care beyond the hospital's comfort level.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider discharge** once the cause is clear, follow-up is arranged and the child is clinically well.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Ataxia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Ataxia/, retrieved 2026-09-23
